governance.residuals_note: RESULT vs the pjm-118 keeper, same recipe: C3c price_tail FAIL -> PASS. Tail hours >$200 (any-zone, the scorer's own basis): 2023 5 h (actual 6), 2024 9 h (actual 18), 2025 39 h (actual 59) -- versus the keeper's 2024 1 h and 2025 15 h. 2024 lands on EXACTLY the pjm-114 east-cut value (9 h) and 2025 within one hour of it (39 vs 40), independently confirming on two years that the cut was off in the registered keeper. C1 fuel-mix 16/16 (free 12/12), C2/C3b/C4/C5a PASS -- unchanged. C3a mean LMP is the SOLE remaining FAIL and is NOT explained by the overlays: 2023 +4.7% PASS / 2024 -3.8% PASS / 2025 -10.7% FAIL, versus the keeper's -10.5% -- i.e. C3a-2025 is overlay-neutral, and the June undershoot measures -20.1 $/MWh with the cut FULLY LIVE (the pjm-118 attestation attributed -19.9 to an unconstrained west->east wheel; that attribution is refuted). Attribution rests where the pjm-117 A/B put it: base arm (gas_offer_net_revenue_margin OFF) -9.4% PASS -> margin arm ON -10.6% FAIL. The ~1.2 pp crossing the +/-10% band is the measured cost of that owner-promoted structure, not a missing overlay and not an unmodelled outage. Re-measured residual for the next lane: the model now reaches the EXTREME tail (39 of 59 hours >$200, max $376) while running ~$20/MWh light on the June mean -- a summer SHOULDER-hour price level miss, not a scarcity-formation failure. The handoff's three proposed lanes (CT/CC <5-day outage intake, seam import abundance, reserve-curve steepness) were all scoped against the missing tail and are moot as framed. No lever was tuned to any residual in this run (rules 1/11/13): the recipe is byte-identical to pjm-118's.
